subject.title: fix(hooks): wire message:sending internal hook to user-defined hooks

question: Should standalone `HOOK.md` automation gain a documented observation-only `message:sending` event, or should all pre-send behavior remain exclusive to typed plugin hooks?
rationale: Current docs explicitly assign outbound cancellation, rewriting, priorities, and ordered policy to typed hooks, while this PR would establish a new standalone internal event and underscore alias without an approved contract.

options.title: Keep pre-send typed-only
options.body: Retain typed plugin hooks as the sole pre-send policy surface, use `message:sent` for standalone audit hooks, and close or substantially narrow this PR.

options.title: Approve an observation event
options.body: Define a colon-keyed, observation-only `message:sending` event that runs once after typed policy and before platform send, with docs, compatibility handling, and live proof.

options.title: Design mutable standalone hooks
options.body: Pause this PR and separately design priority, timeout, merge, cancellation, and failure semantics before exposing standalone hooks as guardrails.

recommendation.title: Keep pre-send typed-only
recommendation.body: Retain typed plugin hooks as the sole pre-send policy surface, use `message:sent` for standalone audit hooks, and close or substantially narrow this PR.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the active exactly-once typed-hook design across the same delivery boundary and are best placed to reconcile the two contracts.
